title: My security
subtitle: Your risk score, the risks your own actions created and what you reported.
notice: These trainings were assigned because of a specific gap. Finishing the training closes the risk.
retakeHint: You finished this training earlier. Complete the whole training again from the start to close this risk.

why.title: What makes up your score
why.hint: Each part adds points; 0 is the best possible score.

report.ctaBody: A strange email, text, call, link or file? Tell the security team. Each report earns {xp} XP.
report.title: Report something suspicious
report.description: The security team checks every report. Don't forward the message or open attachments.
report.subject: What happened?
report.subjectPlaceholder: For example: email from "Accounting" asking to confirm my payslip
report.detailsPlaceholder: Sender, time, what it asked you to do…
report.urlHint: Paste it as text. We never open it.
report.thanks: Thank you. Report TR-{number} is with the security team.
report.thanksXp: Thank you. Report TR-{number} is with the security team. +{xp} XP
report.simulation: Well spotted: that was a training simulation. +{xp} XP
report.simulationNoXp: Well spotted: that was a training simulation. You have already earned today's reporting bonus.

errors.subject: Describe what happened in a few words.

sandbox.title: Sandbox
sandbox.subtitle: Check a suspicious link or file safely before you open it.
sandbox.cardBody: Static analysis: nothing is opened or run.
sandbox.modeBody: The file is not run or stored: only its SHA-256 hash and the findings are kept. Links are not opened; only the address is checked.
sandbox.fileDrop: Drop the file here or <pick>choose it from your computer</pick>
sandbox.fileHint: Up to 10 MB · the file is not run or stored
sandbox.urlHint: The link is not opened: only the address itself is checked.
urlChecks: IP address instead of a domain
sandbox.escalate: Send to the incident response team
sandbox.escalated: Sent to the incident response team.

verdictBody.clean: We found nothing alarming. Stay careful: static analysis can't see everything.
verdictBody.suspicious: Several warning signs. Don't open it; ask the security team.
verdictBody.malicious: This looks dangerous. Don't open it and send it to the incident response team.

errors.tooBig: The file is larger than 10 MB.
errors.rateLimited: Too many checks. Try again in a few minutes.

url.script_scheme: The link runs a script instead of opening a page.
url.unparseable: The address can't be read as a normal link.
url.no_tls: Unencrypted HTTP: anything you type can be read on the way.
url.userinfo_redirect: An “@” hides the real destination: everything before it is ignored.
url.ip_host: A bare IP address instead of a domain name.
url.punycode: Encoded international characters can imitate a known domain.
url.homoglyph_case: Mixed letters like a capital “I” posing as an “l” in {host}.
url.risky_tld: The .{tld} zone is often used for throw-away scam sites.
url.shortener: A link shortener ({host}) hides the real destination.
url.deep_subdomains: Many sub-domains: the real domain is pushed to the end.
url.brand_lookalike: Uses the name “{brand}” but isn't the brand's real domain.
url.lure_words: Bait words such as “{word}” in the address.
url.double_extension: A file with a double extension in the link.
url.direct_download: Downloads a program or script directly.
url.encoded_host: Encoded characters in the domain name.

file.rtlo: A hidden right-to-left character reverses the file name.
file.double_extension: Looks like a .{shown} but is really a .{real} file.
file.disguised_archive: Looks like a .{shown} but is an archive (.{real}).
file.risky_type: The .{ext} file type can run code on your computer.
file.lnk: A Windows shortcut (.lnk) that can start commands.
file.powershell: Contains PowerShell commands (hidden window, encoded or downloading code).
file.lolbin: Calls system tools often abused by attackers (mshta, rundll32, certutil…).
file.disk_image: A disk image (ISO/IMG) used to slip past security marks.
file.pdf_autoaction: The PDF does something automatically when opened.
file.pdf_launch: The PDF tries to launch another program.
file.pdf_embedded: The PDF has an embedded file.
file.remote_template: The document loads a template from the internet when opened.
file.archive_executable: The archive contains a program or script ({name}).
file.encrypted_archive: A password-protected archive: antivirus can't look inside.
file.html_credential_form: The page asks for a password.
file.html_external_post: The form sends what you type to {host}.
file.html_smuggling: The page builds and downloads a file by itself (HTML smuggling).
file.no_findings: Nothing suspicious found in the structure.
